items.evidence: After page.reload() the spec asserts the total equals the promoted subtotal less 25% and that the Manual breakdown row shows 25% (diff lines 99-103). Both values come from the server, so they would fail if the discount mutation never ran.
AC1, the total, is asserted at lines 89 and 101. AC2, Manual 25% alongside the Promotion row, is asserted at lines 94-96. AC3, persistence after reload, is asserted at lines 99-103.

The spec reuses the existing DraftOrderPage members (total, discountToggle, summary, dialog), create, addProduct and the scenario constants. The new members (addDiscountButton, discount inputs, discountRow, addPercentageDiscount) have no existing equivalent.
There are no fixed waits. The new method waits for the dialog to close (diff line 42), and the spec uses web-first assertions.
test and expect are imported from fixtures/test.ts (line 54), the test is not tagged parallel(), and nothing is written to the cache or the dumps.

The spec uses the data-test-ids discount-value and discount-reason, which exist in DiscountFormFields.tsx. Elements without a test id (Add Discount, the Percentage radio, list items) are found by role and name. Locators are scoped to the dialog or the summary, including the submit button.
The ORDERS_SCENARIO data is used. The draft is started with DraftOrderPage.create and addProduct, which is the suite's own pattern, and the discount is the action under test.
There are no hard-coded ids. Every amount is derived from PRODUCTS.tee.price and PROMOTIONS.catalogue.percent.
The spec signs in through the fixture's default admin session. There is no UI login and no credentials appear in the spec.
typecheck.txt reports exit 0 with no errors. The spec is at e2e/tests/orders/draft-manual-discount.spec.ts.
The new locators and the multi-step discount flow are on DraftOrderPage. The spec only calls page-object members, apart from page.reload().

The new fields are readonly and built from this.page via summary or dialog (lines 9-15). The existing constructor(readonly page: Page) {} is kept. discountRow is a parameterised method, as the suite already does for create and addProduct.
The spec has // Arrange (line 72) and // Act & Assert (line 86).
It is one test, with a test.step for each stage (lines 87, 93, 99).
The title says what behaviour is checked and carries the #e2e tag (line 69).
A header comment at lines 58-62 says what the spec covers and why.
Every assertion is a web-first toHaveText or toContainText on a locator.
Expected values are derived from PRODUCTS and PROMOTIONS, guarded by the threshold check at line 80, and money is compared with toFixed(2). The scenario name is imported. The 25% is a named constant.
There is no cleanup code and no unique or random names.
There are no custom timeouts or retries, and no networkidle or waitForLoadState.
Relative imports keep the .ts extension, and test and expect come only from the fixture.
There is no any, no cast and no gql call. The method parameters are typed.
The comments explain reasons (why the toggle is opened first, the hasNot filter, the arithmetic guard) rather than narrating the next line.

structured_output.summary: Submission ca85e605 meets all 23 checklist items. I read the diff and the type-check output and ran nothing. It extends DraftOrderPage with role and test-id locators for the discount dialog and a scoped breakdown-row helper. The single-story spec derives amounts from the scenario constants and guards its arithmetic. It proves persistence by reloading the page and re-asserting the total and the Manual 25% row. The type check passes.
